properties.description: Activation process transforming NiFe oxide to NiFeOOH

nodes.name: Electrochemical Anodic Conditioning
nodes.procedure: We selected NiFe oxide with a nanocage morphology as a precatalyst. These nanocages possess an open structure with wall thicknesses ranging from 10 to 20 nm and exhibit uniform elemental distributions. The NiFe oxide precatalyst was subjected to electrochemical anodic conditioning (AC) at 1.6 V_RHE for 50 h, resulting in its conversion to NiFeOOH, as evidenced by the lattice fringe of approximately 0.213 nm, corresponding to the (103) plane of NiFeOOH. High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) coupled with electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping demonstrates the preservation of the homogeneous elemental distributions throughout the well-maintained nanocage structure during this conversion.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows NiFe oxide nanocage precatalyst with wall thicknesses ranging from 10 to 20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These nanocages possess an open structure with wall thicknesses ranging from 10 to 20 nm and exhibit uniform elemental distributions (Figure 1a and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringe of approximately 0.213 nm corresponding to the (103) plane of NiFeOOH after AC activation; post-RPP treatment reveals pronounced increase in surface roughness and surface amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe oxide precatalyst was subjected to electrochemical anodic conditioning (AC) at 1.6 VRHE for 50 h, resulting in its conversion to NiFeOOH, as evidenced by the lattice fringe of approximately 0.213 nm, corresponding to the (103) plane of NiFeOOH (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM coupled with EELS mapping demonstrates preservation of homogeneous elemental distributions throughout the well-maintained nanocage structure with no noticeable phase segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) coupled with electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping demonstrates the preservation of the homogeneous elemental distributions throughout the well-maintained nanocage structure during this conversion, with no noticeable phase segregation (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Fe K-edge XANES spectra confirm conversion to iron oxyhydroxide features; operando Q-XAFS shows Fe oxidation state remaining ~2.7 during OER, decreases to ~2.2 during RPP, restores to initial during post-RPP OER; Ni oxidation state stable ~2.3 throughout.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A series of Fe K-edge and Ni K-edge XANES spectra acquired during the first stage exhibited minimal variations, with the oxidation state of Fe remaining around 2.7 and that of Ni around 2.3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando quick-scan and conventional EXAFS at Fe K-edge shows Fe-O coordination number stable at 5.2±0.1 during initial OER, decreases to 4.2 during RPP, gradually increases but remains undercoordinated during post-RPP OER; Ni-O CN stable at 4.5±0.3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding EXAFS analysis indicated a stable CN of 5.2±0.1 for the Fe-O path and 4.5±0.3 for the Ni-O path during the first stage (Figure 2d-f).

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge soft-XAFS reveals RPP weakens metal-oxygen bonds, suggesting formation of oxygen vacancies or activation of lattice oxygen.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the O K-edge soft XAFS results reveal that RPP weakens metal-oxygen bonds (Figure 3a), suggesting the formation of oxygen vacancies or the activation of lattice oxygen.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi-in situ XPS shows RPP preferentially reduces Fe over Ni and induces generation of oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi-in situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) data indicate that the RPP treatment preferentially reduces Fe over Ni (see Fe 2p in Figure 3b and Ni 2p XPS spectra in Figure S15) while inducing the generation of oxygen vacancy.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows higher ratio of 474 to 690 cm⁻¹ (ΔI₂) and 556 to 690 cm⁻¹ (ΔI₁) for RPP-OER-treated NiFeOOH, indicating more extensive transformation into catalytically active phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed surface amorphization is closely associated with a more extensive transformation into the catalytically active phase, as revealed by in situ Raman spectroscopy (Figure 3f-h), showing a higher ratio of 474 to 690 cm⁻¹ (ΔI₂) and 556 to 690 cm⁻¹ (ΔI₁) for RPP-OER-treated NiFeOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform analysis of EXAFS confirms conversion to NiFeOOH and preferential formation of undercoordinated Fe sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The conversion to NiFeOOH is further evidenced by X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy and wavelet transform (WT) analysis (Figure 1d-f and S3).
